source.citation: Live capture against the A4H sandbox appliance (SID A4H, client 001) on 2026-08-11 at 2026-08-11T13:06:06Z. Raw capture artifacts (session scratchpad, not committed): wire39b/inj_space.body (408 B, sha256 c209595c98e508451bf380dbda8635928c3537a812c5262b23171a7ce031db8e), wire39b/inj_space.hdr (verbatim response status line + headers), wire39b/inj_space.json (request sidecar), produced by wire39b/cap.sh.
source.notes: SECURITY EVIDENCE, second half of the injection pair (see ddic-injection-where-executed-200). ddicEntityName=T000 WHERE 1=1 (URL-encoded in the path) returned HTTP 400 with the message 'A Boolean expression was expected in "1=1".' — an ABAP Open-SQL PARSER error about the injected predicate's contents. That is the point: the request did not fail because the name was rejected as an identifier, it failed because the injected text reached the SQL parser and was merely malformed. A 400 here is NOT the server defending itself, and must not be read as one; the 200 in the companion cassette is what the same code path does when the injected predicate happens to be well-formed. Together the two pin that server-side validation of ddicEntityName does not exist. Note the error envelope is identical in shape to ddic-table-not-found-400 (same generic ExceptionDataPreviewGeneral type id), so an injected name cannot be distinguished from a typo'd one by the response alone — another reason validation must happen before the request is issued. Anonymisation: appliance.server is the repo's standing pseudonym for the A4H ApplicationServerName. The appliance's real host name and its container IPv4 are deliberately absent from this file, as is the appliance URL; Authorization / Cookie / X-CSRF-Token request-header values are replaced with placeholders. Response bytes are unmodified. kernelRelease/kernelPatchLevel were read live from GET /sap/bc/adt/system/information on the same day as this capture, not copied from an earlier cassette.
